title: TERMS-Bench
question: Can the agent negotiate a good price?
blurb: The agent haggles over a price with a scripted buyer or seller and never learns how far the other side would go. Some counterparts say little, some bluff, some play hardball. In some markets no good deal exists, and the right move is to walk away. Each model plays the paper's full set of 1,800 negotiations.
footnote: Scores on the Economic Intelligence Index's 0-100 scale, rescaled from the benchmark's own results. The questions below explain the scale.

notes.measures: How much of the possible gain from a deal the agent keeps for itself, and whether it knows when to walk away. A bad deal counts against it.
notes.scoring: The paper measures the share of the possible gain the agent keeps, from 0 to 1. We turn that into a 0-100 score. 0 matches a simple scripted negotiator that gives ground at a fixed pace. 100 means every possible deal closed at the agent's best price.
notes.original: The paper reports the raw share. On that scale GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 both kept 72% of the possible gain, and MiniMax M3 47%. Our score starts from the scripted negotiator instead of from zero, so it shows how much better than that baseline each model bargains. The negotiations and model settings follow the paper.
